newsitem.title: LATVIA: VEREINSBANK SIGNS FIRST CONTRACT, SEES PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: VEREINSBANK SIGNS FIRST CONTRACT, SEES PROFIT.

text.p: The new branch of German Vereinsbank, which began operations on Monday, said it signed its first contract and expects to make a profit in three years.

The branch, part of Vereinsbank's Vereins und West Bank subsidiary, becomes the second Western bank to open in Riga after Societe Generale opened an office here in 1995. The bank will have 35 staff, including eight from Germany.
"We have this week signed our first loan contract on the financing of lumber export," Vereinsbank Riga president Dietrich Schutte told a news conference.
He said the new bank would be trade-related and target the corporate bank but would also get involved in project finance.
"We are in serious business talks with Ventspils but we will release details only as they are completed," Schutte added.
He said that talks in Ventspils were taking place with the town authorities, with the port and companies involved in the tranist business.
The bank said it would boost its share capital from the present 3.9 million lats as it expected its business to grow.
The bank also said that it would become profitable around the end of the decade.
"We have our deadline and we expect to be in profit in the third year of operation," said Rolf Kirchfeld, a member of the board of Vereins und Westbank.
Kirchfeldt also said that the bank was open to working with a local partner but that as it grew it would become more difficult to link up with a Latvian bank.
